network.assessment: PRB load (82.0%) exceeds the 85% congestion threshold during landing flare. Cell CELL-APPROACH-01 is situated only 350 m from the threshold. Proposing candidate actions: ACT-1 (power increase) and ACT-3 (antenna beam downtilt for glideslope clearance).

airspace_safety.observation: Aircraft AERO-402 is in landing_flare on ILS CAT I at 50 ft AGL. 5G Cell CELL-APPROACH-01 is 350 m from runway threshold (120 m lateral offset). 3D slant separation distance is 370.5 m.
airspace_safety.assessment: Simulated baseline altimeter margin is +33.9 dB (minimum 6.0 dB required under CLM-106). A dynamic power boost (+3 dB) reduces margin to +30.9 dB, which violates glide path safety. Antenna downtilt (3°) safely restores margin to +38.4 dB (SIMULATION) while preserving cell coverage.
chain_of_thought: 1. Telemetry Inspection: Aircraft AERO-402 at 50 ft AGL, 3D separation 370.5 m from CELL-APPROACH-01.
2. PFD Simulation (CLM-109): Baseline margin = +33.9 dB; +3 dB boost drops margin to +30.9 dB.
3. Glideslope Safety Standard (CLM-106): Enforcing strict 6.0 dB margin floor. Power increases rejected; downtilt verified safe.
4. Precautionary Guard: Radar altimeter tolerance category is unverified; conservative baseline strictly maintained.

spectrum.observation: 5G Cell CELL-APPROACH-01 operates in band n78 with carriers 3400–3600 MHz. In International, the authorized mid-band 5G spectrum is 3300–3670 MHz under CON-INT-004.
spectrum.assessment: Active band n78 (3400–3600 MHz) complies with national licensing. However, candidate retuning to 4100 MHz (n77) is strictly prohibited: it violates national frequency license CON-INT-004 and abuts the globally protected 4200–4400 MHz aeronautical radionavigation band governed by ITU RR 5.438 (CLM-140). Mandatory 530 MHz separation to radar altimeter band must be strictly preserved.
chain_of_thought: 1. Spectrum Allocation Check: Verified active carriers 3400–3600 MHz within licensed band in International (3300–3670 MHz).
2. Aeronautical Protection: Checked ITU Radio Regulations RR 5.438 and CLM-140; 4200–4400 MHz band has strict exclusive aeronautical allocation.
3. Out-of-Band Emission Review: Enforced CON-INT-001 and CON-INT-004. Proposed 4100 MHz operation flagged as severe non-compliance.
4. Verdict: Authorized n78 operation permitted; 4100 MHz retuning rejected.
spectrum.uncertainty: Exact manufacturer spurious emission filter rolloff curve for cell site gNodeB is unverified.
warnings: 4100 MHz operation violates both national license and proximity boundary

policy_institutional.observation: Scenario jurisdiction is International evaluated as of 2026-10-07. Regulatory authorities include DGCA, Ministry of Civil Aviation, and DoT/WPC. Key instruments identified: DGCA AIC 19/2025 and 5G band licensing conditions.
policy_institutional.assessment: DGCA AIC 19/2025 (CLM-131) has an effective date of 2027-12-31, which is in the future relative to 2026-10-07; it is classified strictly as NOT_YET_IN_FORCE. Under institutional rule CON-IN-004, automated cell reconfigurations that increase emissions near an aerodrome require human ATC / coordinator authorization. Furthermore, GAP-006 notes the absence of numeric runway buffer coordinates in primary circulars, mandating precautionary defaults.
chain_of_thought: 1. Temporal Status Audit: Compared as-of date 2026-10-07 against DGCA AIC 19/2025 effective date (2027-12-31). Formally marked NOT_YET_IN_FORCE.
2. Institutional Authorization (CON-IN-004): Automated RF power boosts near runway approach corridors require human oversight.
3. Policy Gap Identification (GAP-006): Primary circulars lack published numeric exclusion contours around runway thresholds. Precautionary boundary enforced.
4. Verdict: Dynamic power increases require human authorization gate; off-corridor traffic steering (ACT-2) and downtilt (ACT-3) comply with institutional mandates.
policy_institutional.uncertainty: GAP-006: Lack of published numeric exclusion radius around synthetic airport runways in primary circulars.
warnings: DGCA AIC 19/2025 is NOT_YET_IN_FORCE as of 2026-10-07

optimization.assessment: Close low-altitude flare geometry (<500 m to runway) requires immediate RF beam shaping. Antenna downtilt combined with PRB power capping provides optimal Pareto protection.
chain_of_thought: 1. Multi-Objective Formulation: Mapped candidate actions onto 4 objective dimensions (Airspace Margin, PRB Relief, License Compliance, Latency).
2. Geometry & Flight Phase: Aircraft in landing_flare at 50 ft AGL, cell at 350 m.
3. Pareto Dominance Evaluation: ACT-2 achieves 0.92 aggregate score; eliminates glideslope interference while recovering QoS.
4. Selection Recommendation: Forwarded ACT-2 as primary preference to arbitration agent.
